package_info.package_versions: All UI builds deployed to IPFS gateways since January 1, 2024
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is considered malicious because a developer surreptitiously inserted JavaScript code into the Tornado Cash user interface that exfiltrates users’ private deposit notes (which function as private keys) to an external server, enabling theft of user funds. This code was hidden within a governance proposal and affected all users accessing the UI via IPFS gateways.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, specifically when a user initiates deposit or withdrawal actions through the UI
execution_context.file_location: Tornado Cash UI JavaScript source code (malicious code injected via governance proposal, present in builds deployed to IPFS gateways)
required_permissions: Network access (to perform outbound HTTPS requests)
Access to in-memory deposit notes (private keys) generated or handled by the UI

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user interacts with deposit or withdrawal functions, the code accesses the user's private deposit note, encodes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive credentials and enabling theft of user funds.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is suspicious because it covertly accesses sensitive user secrets (deposit notes/private keys) and transmits them to an external, attacker-controlled server without any legitimate reason or user notification.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: The legitimate Tornado Cash UI should never transmit private deposit notes or keys off-device or to any third party. The presence of code that exfiltrates these secrets directly violates user privacy and the security model of the application.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry might send anonymized, non-sensitive usage data, but there is no valid reason for any code to transmit private keys or deposit notes. Such behavior is never acceptable in secure DeFi applications.
key_indicators: Direct access to in-memory deposit notes or private keys within the UI code
Encoding and outbound network transmission of sensitive secrets to a hardcoded, non-official external domain
Absence of user notification or consent for the data transfer
Malicious code introduced via a governance proposal (supply chain attack vector)
Network requests to domains not associated with the official Tornado Cash infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the Tornado Cash UI codebase via a deceptive governance proposal and deployed to IPFS gateways.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious code in users' browsers when they interact with the UI.

attack_chain.action: When a user interacts with deposit or withdrawal functions, the malicious code captures the user's private deposit note.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of the deposit note to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: The encoded deposit note is sent via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains the ability to access and steal user funds.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in DeFi UIs that accesses deposit notes or private keys and transmits them to external, non-official domains
Network requests from the UI to hardcoded domains not associated with Tornado Cash, especially during sensitive user actions (deposit/withdrawal)
Obfuscated or hidden code introduced via governance or community proposals, particularly in open-source DeFi projects
file_indicators: Unexpected or unauthorized changes in Tornado Cash UI JavaScript files deployed to IPFS gateways
Functions or code blocks that serialize and transmit deposit notes or private keys
References to external domains (e.g., 'attacker-server.com') not associated with Tornado Cash in the UI source code
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from the UI to attacker-controlled domains such as https://attacker-server.com/collect
Outbound traffic from user browsers containing encoded deposit notes or similar secrets during DeFi interactions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor DeFi UI codebases for any code that accesses and transmits deposit notes, private keys, or other sensitive secrets to external domains. Employ both static and dynamic analysis to flag JavaScript that performs network requests with sensitive data. Track and alert on unauthorized changes in open-source repositories, especially those introduced via governance proposals. On the network side, monitor for and alert on POST requests from user browsers to non-official domains during deposit or withdrawal actions in DeFi UIs.
